questions.prompt: A kernel moves 6.8 MB from DRAM in 20,000 cycles on the GW-1 (341.3 B/cycle peak). DRAM speed of light, in %?
questions.explanation: 6.8e6 / 341.3 ≈ 19,922 cycles of DRAM work in 20,000 cycles.

questions.prompt: DRAM SOL is 95% and sectors per request is 32 for 4-byte loads. What's going on?
options: DRAM is saturated, but mostly with bytes nobody asked for: fix the access pattern
questions.explanation: 4 sectors per request would be coalesced; 32 means each lane gets its own sector.

questions.prompt: Every SOL percentage is below 20%. What kind of problem is it most likely?
options: Latency: not enough work in flight to keep any unit busy
questions.explanation: Nothing is busy, so the kernel is waiting.

questions.prompt: The top stall reason is "MIO throttle / short scoreboard". Where do you look first?
options: Shared-memory access patterns and bank conflicts
questions.explanation: Those stalls are about the shared-memory pipeline.

questions.prompt: Why not time a kernel while profiling it?
options: Profilers replay the kernel to collect counters, which distorts timing
questions.explanation: Measure time and counters in separate runs.
